title: Coherent functors and transformations on common-stage pair categories
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $I=\mathsf{FinExt}_\ell$ be the small directed poset of finite intermediate fields [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set], using [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(\mathcal A_E,U_{F/E},a^A)$ and $(\mathcal B_E,V_{F/E},a^B)$ be diagrams of additive categories [def-weil-additive-category], with additive transition functors [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], identity transitions $U_{E/E}=1$ and $V_{E/E}=1$, and specified natural associator isomorphisms $a^A_{G,F,E}:U_{G/F}U_{F/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{G/E}$ and $a^B_{G,F,E}:V_{G/F}V_{F/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}V_{G/E}$ for $E\subseteq F\subseteq G$. Assume the associators with a repeated adjacent field are identities and the pentagon equations hold. Form their pair categories $P_A,P_B$: objects of $P_A$ are $(E,K)$ with $K\in\mathcal A_E$; morphisms from $(E,K)$ to $(F,L)$ are represented over $M\supseteq E,F$ by common-field maps $u:U_{M/E}K\to U_{M/F}L$, modulo equality after further transport $u_N=a^A_{N,M,F,L}U_{N/M}(u)(a^A_{N,M,E,K})^{-1}$, and likewise for $B$; identities, sums and composites are calculated at one common stage. These prescriptions are well-defined additive categories.

Let $\Phi_E:\mathcal A_E\to\mathcal B_E$ be additive functors with natural isomorphisms
$$b_{F/E}:V_{F/E}\Phi_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_F U_{F/E}.$$
Assume $b_{E/E}=1$ and the tower equation
$$b_{G/E}\circ(a^B_{G,F,E}\Phi_E)=(\Phi_G a^A_{G,F,E})\circ(b_{G/F}U_{F/E})\circ(V_{G/F}b_{F/E}).$$
Then the formulas
$$\Phi(E,K)=(E,\Phi_EK),\qquad
 \Phi[M,u]=[M,b_{M/F,L}^{-1}\circ\Phi_M(u)\circ b_{M/E,K}]
$$
define an additive functor $P_A\to P_B$, independent of the representative and common field. If $\Psi_E$ is another such family with comparisons $c$, and natural transformations $\eta_E:\Phi_E\Rightarrow\Psi_E$ satisfy
$$\eta_F U_{F/E}\circ b_{F/E}=c_{F/E}\circ V_{F/E}\eta_E,$$
then the components $[E,\eta_{E,K}]$ give a natural transformation $\Phi\Rightarrow\Psi$. Identities, composition of functor families with the composite comparisons, and equations of compatible transformations are preserved by this construction. The descended functors and transformations extend to $\Kar(P_A)\to\Kar(P_B)$ [def-weil-karoubi-envelope]: a functor sends $(P,p)$ to $(\Phi P,\Phi p)$ and a transformation has component $\Psi(p)\eta_P\Phi(p)$.

proof.text:
Fix objects $X=(E,K)$ and $Y=(F,L)$. Write $x_M=U_{M/E}K$, $y_M=U_{M/F}L$, and $\alpha^X_{N,M}=a^A_{N,M,E,K}$ (and similarly for $Y$). On $H_M(X,Y)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_M}(x_M,y_M)$ put $t^A_{N,M}(u)=\alpha^Y_{N,M}U_{N/M}(u)(\alpha^X_{N,M})^{-1}$. Normalization gives $t^A_{M,M}=1$. For $M\subseteq N\subseteq H$, the pentagon says
$$\alpha^X_{H,N}U_{H/N}(\alpha^X_{N,M})=\alpha^X_{H,M}a^A_{H,N,M,x_M}.$$
Substitution into $t^A_{H,N}t^A_{N,M}(u)$ gives
$$\alpha^Y_{H,M}a^A_{H,N,M,y_M}U_{H/N}U_{N/M}(u)(a^A_{H,N,M,x_M})^{-1}(\alpha^X_{H,M})^{-1}=t^A_{H,M}(u),$$
where the equality is the naturality equation for $a^A_{H,N,M}$. Thus transport is transitive. These computations use only the assumed pentagon and naturality, and apply verbatim to $B$.

proof.text:
The groups $H_M(X,Y)$ and bilinear composition are supplied by preadditivity. Since $U_{N/M}$ is additive and composition is bilinear,
$$t^A_{N,M}(u+v)=t^A_{N,M}(u)+t^A_{N,M}(v),\quad t^A_{N,M}(0)=0.$$
For composable maps $u:x_M\to y_M$ and $v:y_M\to z_M$, cancellation of the two middle associators gives
$$t^A_{N,M}(vu)=t^A_{N,M}(v)t^A_{N,M}(u),\qquad t^A_{N,M}(1_{x_M})=1_{x_N}.$$
The same statements hold for $B$.

proof.text: The overfields $M\supseteq E,F$ form a nonempty directed poset: $EF$ is one and the compositum of any two is another. Steps 1 and 2 therefore give a directed system of abelian groups $H_M(X,Y)$. Its directed colimit has exactly the representatives and eventual-equality rule in the statement, by the concrete description of [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups]. In particular eventual equality is an equivalence relation and the Hom quotient is an abelian group. Its addition is $[M,u]+[N,v]=[H,t_{H,M}u+t_{H,N}v]$ for $H\supseteq M,N$, its inverse is $[M,-u]$, and its zero is $[M,0]$. Smallness of the index and the stipulated universe bound ensure these are Hom sets. This reasoning applies separately to $A$ and $B$.

proof.text: Define $[N,v][M,u]=[H,t_{H,N}(v)t_{H,M}(u)]$ for $H\supseteq M,N$. If any representative or $H$ changes, choose one upper bound of the finitely many stages and of the witnesses for the changed representatives. Such an upper bound exists by applying directedness repeatedly. Step 1 identifies iterated transport with direct transport, and Step 2 identifies transported composites with composites of transported maps; at this upper bound both proposed answers are literally equal. Thus composition descends. The identity at $(E,K)$ is $[E,1_K]$: its transport to $H$ is $1_{U_{H/E}K}$, so both identity equations hold. Represent three composable classes at one upper bound. Associativity there gives $[H,w(vu)]=[H,(wv)u]$, proving associativity in the quotient. Similarly the two bilinearity equations hold at that upper bound, by preadditivity at the stage. Thus both pair constructions are preadditive categories.

proof.text: To obtain a zero object, take $(E,0_E)$ at any stage (there is one since the index is nonempty). For an additive transition, $1_{U_{M/E}0_E}=U_{M/E}(1_{0_E})=U_{M/E}(0)=0$. An object $Z$ with $1_Z=0$ has exactly one arrow to or from any object, since $f=f1_Z=f0=0$ and $g=1_Zg=0g=0$. Consequently all the Hom classes to and from $(E,0_E)$ are zero. For $X=(E,K)$ and $Y=(F,L)$ choose $M\supseteq E,F$ and set $Q=(M,U_{M/E}K\oplus U_{M/F}L)$. Represent its two inclusions and projections at $M$ by those of the displayed stage biproduct. At $M$ they obey $p_ri_s=\delta_{rs}$ and $i_1p_1+i_2p_2=1_Q$, so the same equalities hold for their classes. This is precisely the biproduct criterion in [def-weil-additive-category]. Hence $P_A,P_B$ are additive categories.

proof.text:
For the functor formula write $b_M^X=b_{M/E,K}$, and use $\alpha^{A,X}_{N,M}$ and $\alpha^{B,\Phi X}_{N,M}$ for the two associators, the latter evaluated on $\Phi_EK$. Define
$$D_M(u)=(b_M^Y)^{-1}\Phi_M(u)b_M^X.$$
The tower equation, evaluated at $K$, is exactly
$$b_N^X\alpha^{B,\Phi X}_{N,M}=\Phi_N(\alpha^{A,X}_{N,M})b_{N/M,x_M}V_{N/M}(b_M^X).$$
Insert this equality and its inverse for $X,Y$ into $D_N(t^A_{N,M}u)$; cancellation gives
$$\alpha^{B,\Phi Y}_{N,M}V_{N/M}((b_M^Y)^{-1})(b_{N/M,y_M})^{-1}\Phi_N(U_{N/M}u)b_{N/M,x_M}V_{N/M}(b_M^X)(\alpha^{B,\Phi X}_{N,M})^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $b_{N/M}$ replaces the middle three factors by $V_{N/M}(\Phi_Mu)$, leaving exactly $t^B_{N,M}(D_Mu)$. This proves the required transport compatibility without strictifying either diagram.

proof.text:
If $[M,u]=[N,v]$, choose an upper bound $H$ witnessing $t^A_{H,M}u=t^A_{H,N}v$. Step 6 gives $t^B_{H,M}D_Mu=D_H(t^A_{H,M}u)=D_H(t^A_{H,N}v)=t^B_{H,N}D_Nv$. Hence the formula on classes is independent of all representatives. At one common stage,
$$D_M(vu)=(b_M^Z)^{-1}\Phi_M(v)\Phi_M(u)b_M^X=D_M(v)D_M(u),$$
and $D_M(u+v)=D_Mu+D_Mv$ by additivity and bilinearity. Finally $D_E(1_K)=1_{\Phi_EK}$ because $b_{E/E}=1$. Therefore the object and arrow formulas in the statement define an additive functor.

proof.text:
Let $\Psi,c,\eta$ be as in the statement. The component at $X=(E,K)$ is $[E,\eta_{E,K}]$. At a common stage $M$, its representative is $V_{M/E}(\eta_{E,K})$, since the repeated-field associators are identities. Write $\eta_M(x_M)$ for $\eta_{M,U_{M/E}K}$. The assumed compatibility gives
$$V_{M/E}(\eta_{E,K})=(c_M^X)^{-1}\eta_M(x_M)b_M^X.$$
For $u:x_M\to y_M$, substitution at source and target and stage naturality give
$$V_{M/F}(\eta_{F,L})D_M^\Phi(u)=(c_M^Y)^{-1}\eta_M(y_M)\Phi_M(u)b_M^X=(c_M^Y)^{-1}\Psi_M(u)\eta_M(x_M)b_M^X=D_M^\Psi(u)V_{M/E}(\eta_{E,K}).$$
This is naturality for every class $[M,u]$, so these components define the asserted natural transformation.

proof.text:
Identity transformations satisfy the compatibility equation because both sides are $b_{F/E}$, and their descended components $[E,1_{\Phi_EK}]$ are identities. If $\eta:\Phi\Rightarrow\Psi$ and $\delta:\Psi\Rightarrow\Omega$ have comparisons $b,c,r$, then
$$(\delta_F\eta_F)U_{F/E}\,b_{F/E}=\delta_FU_{F/E}\,c_{F/E}\,V_{F/E}\eta_E=r_{F/E}\,V_{F/E}(\delta_E\eta_E).$$
Thus their composite is compatible, and its descended component is $[E,\delta_{E,K}\eta_{E,K}]=[E,\delta_{E,K}][E,\eta_{E,K}]$. Any equality between compatible transformations is componentwise an equality at each $E,K$ and remains an equality of these classes. In particular composites occurring in equations are preserved.

source.place: Compatible transformations: identities, vertical composition and equations; independent calculation by the worker (cited blueprint file unavailable on this machine)

proof.text:
For composition of functor families let $\Theta_E:\mathcal B_E\to\mathcal C_E$ have comparisons $d_{F/E}:W_{F/E}\Theta_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\Theta_FV_{F/E}$. The composite comparisons are
$$e_{F/E}=\Theta_F(b_{F/E})\,d_{F/E,\Phi_E}.$$
They are identities for $F=E$. Expand $e_{G/E}(a^C_{G,F,E}\Theta_E\Phi_E)$. First the tower for $d$, then that for $b$, rewrite it as
$$(\Theta_G\Phi_G a^A_{G,F,E})(\Theta_G b_{G/F}U_{F/E})(\Theta_GV_{G/F}b_{F/E})(d_{G/F}V_{F/E}\Phi_E)(W_{G/F}d_{F/E}\Phi_E).$$
Naturality of $d_{G/F}$ at the morphism $b_{F/E}$ replaces the middle pair $\Theta_GV_{G/F}b_{F/E}\cdot d_{G/F}V_{F/E}\Phi_E$ by $d_{G/F}\Phi_FU_{F/E}\cdot W_{G/F}\Theta_F b_{F/E}$. The resulting expression is precisely
$$(\Theta_G\Phi_G a^A_{G,F,E})(e_{G/F}U_{F/E})(W_{G/F}e_{F/E}).$$
So the composite family is coherent. The identity family has comparisons $1$, and its tower reduces to the equality of the diagram's associator with itself.

source.place: Pair universal construction: composite comparisons and their tower equation; independent calculation by the worker (cited blueprint file unavailable on this machine)

proof.text:
For $u$ at $M$, applying the two descended functors successively gives
$$(d_M^Y)^{-1}\Theta_M((b_M^Y)^{-1}\Phi_M(u)b_M^X)d_M^X=(e_M^Y)^{-1}(\Theta_M\Phi_M)(u)e_M^X.$$
Their object formulas also agree. Thus descent preserves composition of functor families, while the identity family sends $[M,u]$ to itself. Whiskering a compatible transformation by a coherent family has, at $(E,K)$, the ordinary stage component $\Theta_E(\eta_{E,K})$ or $\zeta_{E,\Phi_EK}$: this follows directly by evaluating the descended arrow formula at $M=E$, where the comparisons are identities. For left whiskering, its compatibility equation follows from the explicit chain
$$(\Theta_F\eta_F U)\,\Theta_F(b)d_{\Phi_E}=\Theta_F(cV\eta_E)d_{\Phi_E}=\Theta_F(c)d_{\Psi_E}W(\Theta_E\eta_E),$$
where $U=U_{F/E}$, $V=V_{F/E}$, $W=W_{F/E}$, $b=b_{F/E}$, $c=c_{F/E}$, and $d=d_{F/E}$. The first equality is compatibility of $\eta$, the second is naturality of $d$. For right whiskering, if $\zeta:\Theta\Rightarrow\Omega$ has comparisons $d,r$, the chain is
$$\zeta_F\Phi_FU\,\Theta_F(b)d_{\Phi_E}=\Omega_F(b)\zeta_FV\Phi_E d_{\Phi_E}=\Omega_F(b)r_{\Phi_E}W(\zeta_E\Phi_E).$$
Here the first equality is naturality of $\zeta_F$ at $b$ and the second is its compatibility equation. Hence equations involving those whiskerings also remain componentwise equations after descent.

proof.text: Let $\Phi:P_A\to P_B$ be the functor just constructed. On a Karoubi object $(P,p)$ put $\widehat\Phi(P,p)=(\Phi P,\Phi p)$, and send a Karoubi arrow $u$ to $\Phi u$. These are defined because $(\Phi p)^2=\Phi(p^2)=\Phi p$ and, whenever $u=qup$, $\Phi u=\Phi q\,\Phi u\,\Phi p$. The identity in the envelope is $p$, whose image is $\Phi p$, the identity of the image object. Composition and addition are inherited from $P_A,P_B$, so functoriality and additivity follow from $\Phi(vu)=\Phi v\,\Phi u$ and $\Phi(u+v)=\Phi u+\Phi v$. This proves the extension formula directly from [def-weil-karoubi-envelope], with no idempotent-completeness assumption.

source.place: Karoubi universal construction: extension on objects and arrows; independent calculation by the worker (cited blueprint file unavailable on this machine)

proof.text:
For a descended transformation $\eta:\Phi\Rightarrow\Psi$ define $\widehat\eta_{(P,p)}=\Psi p\,\eta_P\,\Phi p$. Naturality at $p$ gives $\Psi p\,\eta_P=\eta_P\,\Phi p$, and idempotence implies
$$\Psi p\,\widehat\eta_{(P,p)}\,\Phi p=\widehat\eta_{(P,p)}.$$
Thus this is a Karoubi morphism. For $u:(P,p)\to(Q,q)$, the relation $u=qup$ implies $up=u=qu$ (multiply by $p$ or $q$). Consequently
$$\Psi u\,\widehat\eta_{(P,p)}=\Psi u\,\eta_P\,\Phi p=\eta_Q\,\Phi u=\widehat\eta_{(Q,q)}\,\Phi u,$$
using naturality at $u$, and $up=u=qu$. This proves naturality in the envelope. When $p=1_P$ the component is $\eta_P$, so it is the stated extension.

source.place: Karoubi universal construction: sandwiched transformation and naturality; independent calculation by the worker (cited blueprint file unavailable on this machine)

proof.text:
The Karoubi identity transformation has component $\Phi p\,1_{\Phi P}\,\Phi p=\Phi p$, exactly the identity at $(\Phi P,\Phi p)$. If $\delta:\Psi\Rightarrow\Omega$, naturality at $p$ and $p^2=p$ give
$$(\Omega p\,\delta_P\,\Psi p)(\Psi p\,\eta_P\,\Phi p)=\Omega p\,(\delta_P\eta_P)\,\Phi p.$$
Thus composition and every componentwise equation of transformations are preserved. For functors, both $\widehat\Theta\widehat\Phi$ and $\widehat{\Theta\Phi}$ send $(P,p)$ to $(\Theta\Phi P,\Theta\Phi p)$ and an arrow $u$ to $\Theta\Phi u$; the identity functor is likewise unchanged. If additivity of the envelope categories is needed explicitly, their Hom groups are the subgroups $\{u:u=qup\}$, their zero is $(0,0)$, and the biproduct of $(P,p),(Q,q)$ is $(P\oplus Q,\operatorname{diag}(p,q))$. Its inclusions and projections are the stage biproduct maps multiplied by $p$ and $q$; their mixed products are zero and their two diagonal products sum to $\operatorname{diag}(p,q)$, the required identity. This completes all the claims.
